headline: Reading the argument behind the article
overview: The article is the output. For someone who maintains one, the interesting surfaces are the ones readers never open: the revision list, the word-level diff, and the page where the disagreement is recorded.
payoff: He can see exactly which words changed, who changed them, and the reason they gave — without leaving the article's own namespace.

scenes.title: The version the world is reading
scenes.narrative: Tom watches this article. What he sees first is what everyone sees — the current published revision, with no indication on the page of how contested or how recent any of it is.

scenes.title: Every edit, with a name and a reason attached
scenes.narrative: The history is the article's real content: a dated list of revisions, each with an author, a byte delta, and an edit summary. Nothing here is anonymous to the system, and nothing is deleted — only superseded.

scenes.title: Two revisions, picked by hand
scenes.narrative: He marks the current revision and one from a few edits back. The radio columns enforce direction — you cannot compare a revision with itself, and the older column locks out everything newer than your pick.

scenes.title: The change, down to the word
scenes.narrative: The comparison is not a file diff — it highlights the changed words inside the changed sentences, so a one-word substitution in a long paragraph is visible immediately instead of being buried in a wall of identical text.

scenes.title: The disagreement has its own page
scenes.narrative: Edits that need justifying get argued on the talk page rather than in the article. For Tom this is the difference between reverting a change and understanding it — the reasoning is a click away from the text it produced.

moments.caption: I check the talk page first to understand why editors disagree about this change.
I compare sources, revisions, and talk-page arguments before deciding whether the change holds up.
I leave with the reasoning behind the edit, not just the article’s current wording.
